subject.title: Materialize node-host inline interpreter eval before exec approval

question: Should node-host approvals treat a generated, content-bound launcher as the concrete mutable file for exact direct `python -c` and `node -e/--eval` requests?
rationale: Current main deliberately denies runtime forms without one existing file, while this patch creates a new trusted artifact and lifecycle; technical correctness alone does not establish maintainer intent for that boundary.

options.title: Adopt narrow materialization
options.body: Accept the four exact non-Windows forms and own the launcher, retention, and interpreter-identity invariants as supported approval behavior.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed policy
options.body: Continue denying approval-backed inline eval and rely on sandbox or explicit full-trust execution for one-liners.

options.title: Land a smaller first slice
options.body: Limit support to one runtime or platform until owner-reviewed real-host proof covers the reduced lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Adopt narrow materialization
recommendation.body: Accept the four exact non-Windows forms and own the launcher, retention, and interpreter-identity invariants as supported approval behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is authorship of the current fail-closed interpreter-approval boundary and trust-model wording.
